content:
According to the latest report from Bloomberg, Apple is less than two weeks away from unveiling a brand-new smart display. The report also revealed design details of this highly anticipated smart home hub device.

Bloomberg pointed out that this home hub will feature a 6-inch square screen, with an overall design reminiscent of the classic iMac G4 — the latter of which used a hemispherical dome base with a metal arm supporting the screen.

According to Mark Gurman, the device's thickness is "similar to an iPhone," with quarter-inch black bezels similar to older iPads. The corners of the body are rounded, "with no sharp edges at all."

Below are more design details revealed in the report:

  • The body adopts Apple's "standard gray aluminum appearance," with "rubber material on the bottom for added stability when placed down."
  • The device features a USB-C port for power supply, with no built-in battery, so it must remain connected to a power source at all times.
  • The bottom is a "metal circular base, featuring multiple rings of perforated speaker grilles."
  • The screen connects to the base via a "polished metal arm."
  • Users can tilt the screen forward or backward to adjust the angle.
  • The body has no volume or power buttons.
  • The front features a single FaceTime camera, with no rear camera.

Bloomberg also mentioned that there is a second version of the home hub "designed for wall-mounted use." This version is also powered via USB-C, with a base that is "a slim square design, positioned below the screen, housing speakers and microphones inside." According to reports, the base "sits flush against the wall, located below the screen."

To read the full report, please visit Bloomberg. What are your thoughts on Apple's home hub product? Planning to get one (or even several)? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
